samples.summary: Swallowing a failed `doc.subscribe` leaves `durable` true, breaking the design's "durable ⇒ reportable" / under-promise rule — and, for the loss event, also breaks archive-on-remove
samples.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `subscribe` and only `console.warn`s; nothing flips the durability state. `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` states the invariant explicitly: "Durable-but-unreportable is worse than uniformly non-durable: it is a guarantee the user cannot see, check, or be warned about when it lapses" (§ Who gets it) and "A failure the store cannot classify still flips `durable` — the default is to under-promise" (§ What the user sees). After a swallowed failure the chip keeps reading `Saved to this device` for a document whose `PersistDisabled`/`LocalChangesDropped` can never be reported. Worse, the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" does not hold for the first subscription: per § Storage, `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` archives only what `expectLoss` latched (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739,757`), and the SDK calls `remove` on every detach — so if the `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently fails, unreconciled work is deleted instead of archived, defeating the Goal "Work that genuinely cannot be reconciled with the server is returned to the user as a document." The safe shape the design asks for is to latch durability off (a lapse reason) when a required durability event cannot be watched, rather than to continue silently.

samples.summary: Design doc not updated for two behavior rules this delta establishes: recovery gated on a successful reconcile (now enforced by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` throwing) and the workspace fallback restricted to HTTP 404
samples.evidence: § Losing work anyway still states the fallback unconditionally: "where the source is gone ... in the first workspace the server still lists for the user. Handing the work back somewhere beats refusing". The code now refuses for anything but a 404 (`offline-runtime.tsx:259`) and refuses the whole offer when the reconcile failed (`offline-runtime.tsx:169`), the latter made load-bearing by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` changing from best-effort-returns-0 to throwing (`offline-erase.ts:476-479`). Those are policy decisions recorded only in code comments; CONTRIBUTING asks that behavior of this kind be folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than left to comments. No user-visible harm — behavior matches intent — so the cost stays inside the codebase.

samples.summary: The 403 branch is largely defensive duplication of the reconcile gate it cites
samples.evidence: A document the user may no longer read is absent from `fetchDocuments()`, so `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (which runs first and must have succeeded for this code to be reached) has already dropped that archive with `archives: "drop"`. The 403 arm is therefore a second line of defence rather than the only one; harmless and cheap, but worth knowing it is not the primary guard the comment implies.

finding.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `subscribe` and only `console.warn`s; nothing flips the durability state. `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` states the invariant explicitly: "Durable-but-unreportable is worse than uniformly non-durable: it is a guarantee the user cannot see, check, or be warned about when it lapses" (§ Who gets it) and "A failure the store cannot classify still flips `durable` — the default is to under-promise" (§ What the user sees). Worse, the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" does not hold for the first subscription: per § Storage, `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` archives only what `expectLoss` latched (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739,757`), and the SDK calls `remove` on every detach — so if the `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently fails, unreconciled work is deleted instead of archived, defeating the Goal "Work that genuinely cannot be reconciled with the server is returned to the user as a document." verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described: `watch()` in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:268-278 swallows a throwing `doc.subscribe` with only a `console.warn`, and no state setter runs, so `durable` (computed at :181 from `lost`/`writesFailing`/`persistDisabled`) stays true and `lapse` (:199-207) stays undefined forever for that document. The quoted design invariants are verbatim in docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:101-107 ("durable ⇒ reportable") and :486-487 ("A failure the store cannot classify still flips `durable` — the default is to under-promise"), so this is a spec-conformance mismatch, in-lane. The secondary claim also checks out: `expectLoss` is called only from the `local-changes-dropped` handler (:282), and wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739-757 archives only what that latch marked while the SDK calls `remove` on every detach — so a silently failed first subscription deletes unreconciled work instead of archiving it, defeating the stated Goal and § Recovery (:510-515). The only version gate, `supportsClientKey()` (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82), controls whether the durable client mounts at all and does not make the throw path unreachable; the component's own comment (:260-267) asserts the throw is reachable on pins this app can take. No guard elsewhere flips durability on a failed watch. Cost is outside codebase tidiness (chip promises durability it cannot report; unsent work deleted rather than returned), so major is the right grade.
